A LinkedIn post earns attention for about 48 hours, and the author owns nothing from it. LinkedIn owns your followers and the feed decides who sees you. An email list is the one asset that moves with you. A lead magnet under the post turns that rented attention into a subscriber you can reach without any platform's permission. Diandra Escobar's newsletter passed 6,000 readers in four months with 44% open rates and 8% click-through rates, and that list sold 50 seats of The LinkedIn Engine in three days before a single public post existed.

This video covers the full LinkedIn lead magnet system for founders, consultants, and operators: the four mistakes that kill a magnet, the one rule behind every magnet that converts, the $20 test, and four formats worth building (a Claude skill, a Loom walkthrough, copy-paste prompts, and a five day email course). It also covers the deep space habit that feeds the content flywheel, the 11 word follow-up email, and the offer ladder that runs from free content to a $500 consulting call, a $99 a month Skool community, and a done-for-you retainer.

It closes with Magnets, the free tool Diandra and Cam built to replace the landing page, email delivery, and follow-up sequence stack. Magnets hosts the page, sends the resource, runs the sequence, and routes sign-ups to beehiiv, Kit, Slack, Pipedrive, or Zapier.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:
 Why a post with no next step leaves you owning nothing
 The four mistakes that make lead magnets look like they don't work
 The one rule and the $20 test every magnet has to pass
 Four lead magnet formats, including the one that's fastest to build
 How one round of deep thinking becomes videos, posts, and a magnet
 The 11 word email that opens more sales conversations than a pitch
 How to build an offer ladder between free content and a retainer
 How to host a magnet and automate the follow-up without code

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 LinkedIn owns your followers, and your email list is the one asset that moves with you
 A lead magnet solves one specific problem for one specific person in one sitting
 If nobody would pay $20 for the magnet, rebuild it before you ship it
 Build one magnet per idea and let that idea ride across weeks of content
 Each step of the offer ladder sells the next step: the magnet earns the email, the email earns the small offer
 A $500 consulting call credited to the first retainer month means buyers have already paid once and seen a result
